source.title: The Long Delay to Arithmetic Generalization: When Learned Representations Outrun Behavior

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures delayed generalization and internal progress on algorithmic arithmetic tasks, using Collatz prediction and mechanistic probes/interventions rather than the original modular-arithmetic setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own arithmetic-task accuracy trajectories, probes, and interventions. Results cited from prior work are not recorded as rows. Probe values used only to characterize features are included where they bear on the proposed gradual internal progress; optimizer settings alone are not treated as artifact tests.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own delayed-generalization trajectories on Collatz arithmetic (V1). It also tracks probes, erasures, attention and encoder/decoder swaps over training to ask what happens inside the plateau (V2). It is a different method on the same question. It also leans toward T5, because it argues the delay sits in decoder readout rather than in late formation of structure.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the grokking plateau reflects limited readout of structure the encoder already holds, not late acquisition of that structure. They say decoder readout is the dominant bottleneck, shown by transplant and rewind interventions. Readout difficulty depends on numeral base, with binary failing outright. They say the dissociation holds across architectures, task families and scales up to Pythia-1.4B, but evidence is confined to controlled arithmetic tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Studies one-step Collatz and related digit-encoded arithmetic tasks rather than the original small modular-arithmetic dataset setup; uses encoder probes, feature erasure, and encoder/decoder interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Numeral base and local digit structure strongly affect accuracy; decoder depth has a non-monotonic effect; carry exposure changes branch performance; model architecture and scale alter the observed feature/output gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Numeral base strongly sets final learnability, and the ordering survives length-normalized metrics. Bases divisible by 2 and 3 are near ceiling, binary fails, and the same ordering holds for k=-1 and k∈{5,7}.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input representation (numeral base) controls whether and how well arithmetic grokking-like generalization occurs, through the locality of the digit transduction.

fits_no_version.finding: A converged encoder accelerates a fresh decoder, including across bases (base-24 encoder into base-2: 0.751 vs 0.365). A trained decoder does not help a fresh encoder.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The grokking delay in encoder–decoder models is dominated by decoder readout of already-formed features.

record.problems: The principal evidence is from controlled algorithmic arithmetic rather than naturalistic data. The central base-8 setting reports 1,000 sampled integers per training step but no training-accuracy trajectory or training-set-size sweep, so the dataset-shrink portion of V1 is not assessed. Some appendix results are stated without numeric trajectories or uncertainty intervals.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining base-sweep conditions (bases 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 16, 18, 24, 27, 32, 36, and 48) are represented by their overall endpoint values in R17–R30; even- and odd-branch values are omitted because they do not establish the delayed trajectory. Other reported base-specific branch values and detailed k-Collatz, GCD transfer, and carry-exposure results are not separate rows because they do not directly measure the delayed-generalization or gradual-progress behavior named by V1 or V2. Decoder-only zero endpoints for bases 4, 8, 16, and 32 are not itemized separately from R39.

untested.parts: Training-accuracy saturation is not reported; there is no training-set-size sweep; training data are sampled online rather than drawn from a fixed small set.
No Fourier/modular-addition circuit, and no explicit memorizing component whose removal is measured.
No non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
Pythia fine-tuning is on synthetic arithmetic, not realistic data, and shows no delayed jump.
Weight decay is fixed at 1e-2; no critical dataset size or ungrokking test.
Algorithms are not compared across runs. Only the parity-routing head's identity is reported as seed-dependent.
AdamW and FP32 are fixed throughout; no optimizer or numerical controls.

missing.what: Trajectory-resolved erasure hierarchy at 50 checkpoints. Residue-erasure drops peak in the plateau and decay; magnitude-erasure drop rises monotonically to 0.141. The crossover at ~5×10^4 steps marks the readout transition, and the authors call this a mechanistic progress measure.
Seed replication of attention-head specialization: peak single-head shares 0.89, 0.95 and 0.97 in three runs, with the fourth diffuse (peak below 0.50); head identity is seed-dependent.
Short-carry training: odd accuracy plateaus at 38.3% and never recovers. Carry-stratified training leaves odd accuracy at 91.5% but drops even accuracy to 26.9%.
Decoder depth changes delay length. A 1-layer decoder reaches 80% odd accuracy at step 44k versus 102k for depth 4. The depth-4 run shows a transient drop from 88.4% to 74.3% near step 100k.
From-scratch NanoGPT-30M stalls at 0.013 exact-match by step 200k, while Pythia-160M reaches the elbow at least 33× sooner.

record.verdict_notes: Training samples 1,000 integers per step from [1,10,000], with evaluation on 5,000 'unseen' integers. How held-out integers are kept out of training is not explained, and the base-2 text says the model 'memorizes its 1,000 training examples'. The train/test regime is therefore ambiguous relative to the original fixed-small-dataset grokking setup. Pythia fine-tuning shows a smooth closing over ~500 steps rather than a grokking jump. Those rows were mislinked, and R33's value confused the probe–output gap with output accuracy. Weight decay (1e-2) and AdamW are fixed, so V5 and V7 are untested.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training accuracy saturation alongside test accuracy, a fixed small training dataset in the original sense, or a sweep showing that smaller training sets require more optimization.
Does not test a Fourier algorithm for modular addition specifically. It studies Collatz arithmetic and decoder readout, not whether that particular algorithm or account generalizes.
No non-algorithmic image, text, or molecule task, initialization-scale sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition test.
Pythia models are fine-tuned on controlled arithmetic tasks, not evaluated for delayed generalization during realistic LLM pretraining or realistic-data fine-tuning.
No comparison of weight decay or other low-norm bias, circuit efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking threshold.
Does not identify and compare the algorithms learned across runs as a test of whether the same algorithm is recovered.
No controlled test of adaptive-optimizer instability or softmax floating-point limits. Stating the optimizer and precision used is not such a test.

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, base 8
rows.operation_detail: Train on one-step Collatz prediction and evaluate held-out sequence exact-match accuracy.
rows.value: 38% at step 2,000; late jump around step 44k; 97.3% at step 500,000
rows.note: Shows low output accuracy well before a late rise to near-perfect accuracy, but the initial value is not described as chance and training accuracy is not reported here.
rows.check: Plateau starts near 38% because the even branch is learned early (Fig. 1A), so the jump is not from chance; training accuracy is not reported. Online sampling of 1,000 integers per step from [1,10,000] is not a fixed small training set.

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, base 8
rows.operation_detail: Fit linear parity probes to encoder representations across layers.
rows.value: All six layer probes exceed 99.7%; output sequence accuracy at this step is 38%.
rows.note: The probe result establishes early decodability while output behavior remains low; it is not itself evidence that a complete generalizing circuit has formed.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. Early parity decodability alone does not establish gradual formation of a generalizing circuit or subsequent removal of memorizing components.
source_check.problem: The reported probe result is correct, but observed overstates what this measurement establishes about V2.

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, base 8
rows.operation_detail: Probe low-order residues in encoder representations at step 2,000.
rows.value: At layer 5: mod 2 0.997, mod 4 0.995, mod 8 0.996; mod 16 0.982. Probes are near ceiling across layers, with mod 16 weaker in earlier layers.
rows.note: Reports early linear availability of several residue features.

source_check.correct: The listed values belong to layer 0. At layer 5, mod-2 accuracy is 0.998, mod-4 is 0.996, mod-8 is 0.997, and mod-16 is 0.990. State: cannot_determine for V2 from this checkpoint alone.
source_check.problem: The row assigns layer-0 values to layer 5 and treats early feature availability as observation of V2.

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, base 8
rows.operation_detail: Measure conditional probes for successive levels of the 2-adic residue hierarchy.

conditions.value: k2: mod 4 given mod 2; k3: mod 8 given mod 4; k4: mod 16 given mod 8

rows.value: k2 and k3 exceed 0.99 from step 2,000; k4 starts at 0.676 and peaks near 0.96 around step 130,000.
rows.note: The finer conditional residue measure changes gradually while coarser measures are already high.

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, base 8
rows.operation_detail: Project the learned linear parity direction out of encoder hidden states at inference.
rows.value: Accuracy drop peaks at 8.2 percentage points.
rows.note: The paper reports that the parity cue has its strongest causal effect during the plateau.

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, base 8
rows.operation_detail: Project the learned linear parity direction out of encoder hidden states at inference.
rows.value: 0.3 percentage points
rows.note: The parity-direction effect has largely disappeared by this point.
rows.check: The decline from 8.2 to 0.3 pp is the predicted displacement of the plateau-phase parity cue. It belongs to the same trajectory as R5, not a weaker effect.

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, base 8
rows.operation_detail: Erase encoder-side probe subspaces at the converged checkpoint.
rows.value: Residue and last-digit drops are at most 0.001; magnitude drop is 0.141; random controls cost at most 0.005.
rows.note: The authors interpret the result as a shift from a parity-anchored cue to a magnitude-anchored, residue-redundant readout.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix L; Table 9; accompanying trajectory analysis and Fig. 17

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, base 8
rows.operation_detail: Track decoder cross-attention mass on the final input digit.
rows.measure: Share of BOS cross-attention on the last input position
rows.note: The paper places the dispersal within the steepest part of the second loss elbow.

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, base 8, encoder transplant
rows.stage_stated: trained encoder frozen; fresh decoder trained
rows.operation_detail: Freeze a converged encoder and train a freshly initialized decoder.
rows.baseline: Scratch reaches 70% at step 66,000 and converges to 86.1% in the matched-budget comparison.
rows.value: Encoder transplant reaches 70% at step 24,000 and converges to 92.4%.
rows.note: The paper reports the transplant reaches 70% 2.75× earlier than scratch.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. Encoder transplant accelerates behavioral learning, but this comparison does not track formation of a generalizing circuit or removal of memorizing components.
source_check.problem: A transplant speedup localizes a bottleneck without directly observing V2's mechanism.

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, base 8, decoder transplant
rows.stage_stated: trained decoder frozen; fresh encoder trained
rows.operation_detail: Freeze a converged decoder and train a freshly initialized encoder.
rows.value: Accuracy declines over training.
rows.note: The transplanted decoder does not provide the acceleration observed for encoder transplant.
rows.check: Comparator. The absence of acceleration under decoder transplant is the expected asymmetry that localizes the delay. The row's 'absent' wording is misleading.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. Decoder transplant declines over training; its asymmetry with encoder transplant bears on readout compatibility, without measuring gradual circuit formation or memorization removal.
source_check.problem: The comparator does not itself establish observation of V2.

rows.subject: Base-2 model with base-24 encoder transplant
rows.stage_stated: base-24 trained encoder frozen; fresh base-2 decoder trained
rows.operation_detail: Transplant a trained base-24 encoder into a fresh base-2 model.
rows.value: Mean 0.751; standard deviation 0.038
rows.uncertainty: Non-overlapping 95% intervals are reported; per-seed intervals are in Table 3.
rows.note: The transplant exceeds scratch on every seed.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. At step 300,000, cross-base transplant achieves 0.751 ± 0.038 versus scratch 0.365; these endpoints establish transfer benefits rather than V2's temporal mechanism.
source_check.problem: An endpoint transfer comparison cannot establish gradual circuit formation or later memorization removal.

rows.subject: Base-2 model with base-24 encoder transplant
rows.stage_stated: base-24 trained encoder frozen; fresh base-2 decoder trained
rows.operation_detail: Transplant a trained base-24 encoder into a fresh base-2 model.
rows.value: Mean 0.524; standard deviation 0.067
rows.note: The paper reports a roughly fourfold separation on the odd branch.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. Odd-branch transplant accuracy is 0.524 ± 0.067 versus scratch 0.119; this measures transfer performance rather than the temporal mechanism in V2.
source_check.problem: The branchwise endpoint does not observe V2's mechanism.

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, base 8, decoder rewind
rows.stage_stated: converged encoder frozen; decoder reset to step-2k weights and trained
rows.operation_detail: Freeze the converged encoder, rewind the decoder, and train only the decoder.
rows.baseline: Joint training reaches 86.1% over the same budget.
rows.value: Decoder rewind reaches 91.9% by step 22,000 and 97.6% overall.
rows.note: The authors interpret the faster learning with a fixed encoder as evidence that decoder readout is the dominant delay.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. Decoder rewind reaches 91.9% by step 22,000 and 97.6% overall versus 86.1% for joint training; it isolates readout learning without identifying the full generalizing circuit or memorizing components.
source_check.problem: Faster readout learning does not directly establish V2's circuit-development sequence.

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, decoder rewind
rows.stage_stated: fresh decoder trained against a frozen converged encoder
rows.operation_detail: Repeat decoder rewind with five fresh decoder seeds.
rows.note: A fresh decoder reaches slightly above joint-training accuracy without further encoder gradients.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. Five fresh decoder seeds average 0.978 versus joint training 0.969; final accuracies do not track gradual circuit formation or cleanup.
source_check.problem: The endpoint replication establishes encoder sufficiency for retraining, not observation of V2.

rows.subject: 6-layer encoder–decoder transformer, decoder rewind
rows.stage_stated: fresh decoder trained against frozen encoder snapshots
rows.operation_detail: Sweep the frozen encoder snapshot used for decoder rewind.
rows.value: Fresh decoders reach 0.65–0.80, with no meaningful improvement from additional encoder compute; the step-2k snapshot is reported as as good a starting point as step 50k.
rows.note: The authors say the second elbow is not caused by encoder refinement.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. Frozen snapshots at 2k, 10k, 20k, and 50k yield fresh-decoder accuracies of 0.65–0.80 without meaningful improvement across snapshots; this does not track the complete generalizing circuit.
source_check.problem: Snapshot sufficiency does not establish the formation or removal sequence specified by V2.

rows.subject: One-step k=-1 Collatz model, base 8
rows.operation_detail: Train on the k=-1 Collatz variant and report the delayed accuracy trajectory.
rows.value: Below 50% for the first 50,000 steps; 91.0% at convergence, compared with 95.7% for k=3.
rows.note: The text calls this the same qualitative delayed-generalization dynamic; training accuracy and a data-size sweep are not reported.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Probe pretrained and fine-tuned residual-stream features while measuring Collatz output accuracy.
rows.value: T(n) mod 8 and n mod 16 probes are 1.00; output exact-match is 0.000.
rows.note: Task-relevant features are linearly readable before task gradients, while task output is absent.
rows.check: Features are present in the pretrained checkpoint before any task training, and fine-tuning shows no delayed jump. This measures pre-existing features, not gradual circuit formation ahead of a jump.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune all parameters on base-8 Collatz while tracking probes and output accuracy.
rows.baseline: At step 0, probes are 1.00 and output exact-match is 0.000.
rows.value: Output exact-match is 0.85 at step 50, 0.16 at step 200, and 0.02 at step 500; the text says it reaches at least 0.97 by about step 500.
rows.note: The paper describes a smooth early closure of the probe-output gap; the step-500 values are reproduced as stated in the text.
rows.check: Value is wrong. 1.00/0.85/0.16/0.02 at steps 0/50/200/500 is the probe–output gap, not output exact-match. Output is about 0.15 at step 50, 0.845 at step 200 and at least 0.97 by about step 500. The closing is smooth with no plateau-then-jump, so V2's anticipation of a jump cannot be shown.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Project out the probe subspace for n mod 16 before decoding.
rows.value: Probe-subspace erasure leaves accuracy 0.043 (drop 0.802); random subspace costs 0.005.
rows.note: The authors report a causal dependence on the probe-aligned subspace at the layer where probes saturate.
rows.check: Causal-use check during smooth fine-tuning. It is not a progress measure anticipating a delayed jump.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Probe units-digit carry while tracking addition output accuracy.
rows.value: Carry probe is in the 0.78–0.87 band from step 0; exact-match stays below 0.14 for about 2,000 steps.
rows.note: Shows a feature-behavior gap on a second arithmetic task, but the probe is not near-perfect.
rows.check: Carry probe stays flat at 0.78–0.87 while output lags, so it does not track progress toward the jump. The output delay itself is a V1-type observation on fine-tuning, without a jump value given.

rows.subject: Pythia-160M
rows.operation_detail: Probe arithmetic features in the pretrained model while tracking Collatz output accuracy.
rows.value: Best-layer probes are at least 0.98; output exact-match is 0.000.
rows.note: The paper reports the gap at the pretrained checkpoint.
rows.check: Probes are saturated at step 0 of a pretrained model. This says nothing about gradual formation.

rows.subject: Pythia-160M
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune on base-8 Collatz and track output exact-match.
rows.value: At least 0.97 by step 10,000
rows.note: Checkpointing was approximately every 2,000 steps, so the output trajectory is described as coarse.
rows.check: Output trajectory is checkpointed only every ~2,000 steps. §4.4 says plateau-then-elbow, but no plateau values are given.

rows.subject: 12-layer decoder-only transformer, base 8
rows.operation_detail: Probe residues and last-digit features across layers and measure output exact-match.
rows.value: Probes recover mod 2, 4, 8 and last digit at at least 0.999 in early layers; final output exact-match is 0.000.
rows.note: The text says these features later collapse in final layers.
rows.check: The decoder-only model never generalizes, so there is no jump for probes to anticipate.

rows.subject: Decoder-only transformer, base 2
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate final held-out sequence exact-match on Collatz.
rows.note: The paper reports zero final exact-match for each of bases 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32; only this base is itemized here.
rows.check: Linked to the wrong version. Zero final exact-match in the decoder-only model (all five bases, ≥170k steps; base 2 stopped at 95k) is a failure to grok, which bears on V1, not V2.

rows.subject: Encoder–decoder transformers, base 8
rows.operation_detail: Sweep model width and depth while tracking probes and output accuracy.
rows.value: Final exact-match 0.853–0.968; the shadow-knowledge gap and second loss elbow are reported in every configuration, with parity and mod-4 probes at least 0.99 within the first few thousand steps.
rows.note: The text reports the trajectory pattern across all nine configurations as an aggregate.
rows.check: The second elbow in all nine configurations is a V1 delay, and early probes ≥0.99 bear on V2. Only aggregate statements are given, with no per-cell trajectory numbers.

source_check.correct: State: partial for V1; cannot_determine for V2 from this row. All nine configurations show a late elbow, but the stated results do not establish chance-level plateaus or post-training-saturation delays. Early probes alone do not establish V2's circuit-development sequence.
source_check.problem: Observed overstates both the complete V1 trajectory and the mechanism established by early probes.

rows.subject: Pythia-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Erase selected probe subspaces or matched-rank random subspaces at varying layers.
rows.value: At layer 4, n mod 16 drop is 0.373 and last-digit drop is 0.412; the text reports dependence at layer 12 at most 0.18 and at layer 20 at most 0.01.
rows.note: The authors report that dependence on the probed subspaces weakens with depth and that the converged addition readout is distributed.
rows.check: Depth dependence of erasure in a smooth fine-tune. It does not measure gradual formation before a jump.

rows.subject: Frozen one-step Collatz encoder with fresh decoder
rows.stage_stated: converged encoder frozen; fresh decoder trained
rows.operation_detail: Train a fresh decoder on the two-step Collatz iterate T² using a converged one-step encoder.
rows.value: A flat early region with exact-match well below its eventual value, followed by a late elbow.
rows.note: No numeric endpoint or step is stated in the provided text.
rows.check: The plateau-then-elbow occurs even with the encoder frozen. No numbers are stated; it supports a readout-side delay.

source_check.correct: State: partial for V1; cannot_determine for V2. Appendix K reports a qualitative plateau followed by an elbow with a frozen encoder, without a numeric endpoint, chance comparison, training-saturation measurement, or circuit-development trace.
source_check.problem: The qualitative behavioral trajectory establishes only part of V1 and does not directly observe V2.

relationships.condition: Encoder–decoder transformers on base-8 Collatz (k=3 and k=-1), including the 3×3 width/depth sweep
relationships.reason: Accuracy stays low for tens of thousands of steps, then rises late: jump ~44k to 97.3% (R1); below 50% for 50k steps then 91.0% (R31); second elbow in all nine configurations (R40); a frozen-encoder T² run shows the same shape (R42).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy jumped near step 44,000 to 97.3% in one trajectory and reached 91.0% after staying below 50% for 50,000 steps in another, with a second acceleration across all nine configurations and a similar frozen-encoder trajectory.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Encoder–decoder transformers on base-8 Collatz (k=3 and k=-1), including the 3×3 width/depth sweep
source_check.reason: Late generalization is reported, but the main base-8 trajectory begins near 38% after early even-branch learning, qualifying V1's jump from chance. R1 and R31 are already correctly marked partial; training saturation and training-size dependence remain untested.

relationships.reason: The plateau sits near 38%, not chance, because the even branch is learned early; the late jump is concentrated on the odd branch (R1, Fig. 1A).
relationships.display_finding: Overall accuracy plateaued near 38% because the even branch was learned early; the late jump concentrated on the odd branch.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: §4.1 reports 38% output accuracy at step 2,000, and Fig. 1 distinguishes earlier even-branch learning from the later odd-branch improvement.

relationships.reason: Base 2 memorizes, peaks at 56.0%, then collapses to 0 through 500k steps (R16). The decoder-only model reaches 0.000 at every base tested (R39). In both, no late generalization occurs.
relationships.display_finding: Binary encoding peaked at 56.0% before collapsing to zero through 500k steps, while the 12-layer decoder-only model reached 0.000 at every tested base.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: These condition groups explicitly lack delayed generalization: binary collapses to zero through 500k steps, and all five decoder-only bases finish at 0.000. Within these small algorithmic settings, the effect is absent rather than merely weakened.

relationships.reason: Continuous internal measures change through the flat region and align with the elbow (R4–R8). These are a gradual k4 residue probe, parity-erasure dependence peaking in the plateau then fading, the readout shifting to magnitude, and a single parity-routing head dispersing at the elbow. The trajectory-resolved erasure hierarchy that the authors call a progress measure is not captured in the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Residue-probe performance improves gradually, parity dependence peaks then fades, and readout shifts toward magnitude during the plateau, while a parity-routing head disperses at the elbow.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: Appendix D.1 shows gradual fine-residue development; Appendices L and D.3 show changing causal readout dependence and head dispersal. Fig. 17 directly reports continuous internal reorganization during the behavioral plateau. This supports V2's hidden-progress component; identified memorizing-component removal remains untested.

relationships.condition: Base-8 encoder–decoder interventions and cross-base transplant
relationships.reason: Residue features are near ceiling by step 2k rather than forming gradually (R2, R3). Transplanting or rewinding onto a frozen encoder removes or shortens the plateau (R9, R11–R15), and decoder transplant does not (R10). The authors therefore locate the dominant delay in readout, not in formation of a generalizing circuit.
relationships.display_finding: Residue features were near ceiling by step 2k, and transplanting or rewinding onto a frozen encoder shortened or removed the plateau while decoder transplant did not, pointing to a readout bottleneck.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Base-8 encoder–decoder interventions and cross-base transplant
source_check.reason: Early residue features and transplant/rewind benefits establish representation availability and a readout bottleneck. V2 concerns the complete generalizing circuit, which includes readout; these results do not establish that its gradual formation or subsequent memorization cleanup fails.

relationships.condition: Attention-head analysis across four base-8 seeds
relationships.reason: Single-head dominance followed by dispersal at the elbow occurs in 3 of 4 seeds; the fourth stays diffuse, peaking below 0.50 (Table 5). The rows record only the reference run (R8), so this verdict rests on the text.
relationships.display_finding: A dominant attention head dispersed at the elbow in 3 of 4 seeds, while the fourth remained diffuse with a peak below 0.50.

source_check.label: limits_scope

labels.reason: These condition groups explicitly lack delayed generalization: binary collapses to zero through 500k steps, and all five decoder-only bases finish at 0.000. Within these small algorithmic settings, the effect is absent rather than merely weakened.

labels.label: supports
labels.reason: Appendix D.1 shows gradual fine-residue development; Appendices L and D.3 show changing causal readout dependence and head dispersal. Fig. 17 directly reports continuous internal reorganization during the behavioral plateau. This supports V2's hidden-progress component; identified memorizing-component removal remains untested.

labels.condition: Base-8 encoder–decoder interventions and cross-base transplant
labels.reason: Early residue features and transplant/rewind benefits establish representation availability and a readout bottleneck. V2 concerns the complete generalizing circuit, which includes readout; these results do not establish that its gradual formation or subsequent memorization cleanup fails.

relation.reason: Its own behavioral trajectories and mechanistic measurements bear on V1 and V2.

tranche.reason: The study directly investigates delayed arithmetic generalization and hidden progress using digit-encoded Collatz tasks, probes, erasures, and encoder/decoder interventions.

source_check.notes: Appendix I inconsistently claims at least 170k steps for every decoder-only run while explicitly listing 95k for base 2 and 145k for base 4; R39 uses the explicit checkpoint. Transition timings differ across analyses and should not be merged into one synchronized trajectory.

statements.correction: Residues are decodable early; encoder transplants and decoder rewinds improve learning; the authors attribute the dominant bottleneck to readout; head specialization varies across seeds. Complete generalizing circuits and memorizing components are not directly identified, so these interventions do not establish a failure of V2.
statements.problem: The empirical summary is accurate, but the limits_scope interpretation conflates early residue availability with availability of the complete generalizing circuit.
